central_question: Can ORION detect when existing formal languages are inadequate and construct a minimal, semantically grounded, predecessor-recovering formalism that yields protected new consequences beyond strongest existing formal parents?

studies.name: GENERALIZED_OBJECT_AND_CLOSURE_DISCOVERY
studies.design: Generate systems where a useful operation leaves the current object class; compare local exceptions versus a generalized object class with exact closure tests.

studies.name: RELATION_OPERATION_AND_INVARIANT_SYNTHESIS
studies.oracle: generated finite structures with hidden operation laws and invariants

studies.name: SEMANTICS_EQUIVALENCE_AND_COMMON_FRAMEWORK
studies.design: Present rival successful calculi; require explicit translation/equivalence or conclude no faithful common framework.

studies.name: CONSERVATIVE_EXTENSION_AND_PREDECESSOR_RECOVERY
studies.oracle: generated old_theory_new_regime pairs with exact recovery maps

studies.name: FORMALISM_NEEDED_OR_NOT
studies.design: Balanced cases where the correct terminal is new formalism, existing parent, local patch, additional data, or no change.

studies.name: FRESH_MINI_FRONTIER_FORMALISM_GENESIS
studies.design: Generate post-freeze research episodes whose hidden solution requires inventing an intermediate representation/definition before proving or deciding the target; hide generator labels from solvers.

studies.name: REAL_FRONTIER_EXPLORATORY_LANE
studies.design: Apply the mechanism to genuine open mathematical/scientific problems. Candidate definitions/formalisms are retained as hypotheses; a claimed solution requires independent proof checking or empirical validation.

kill_or_contraction_conditions: strongest existing parent resolves the deficit
one local variable or patch resolves the deficit at lower cost
candidate has no prospective new consequence
candidate works only on memorized historical breakthroughs
no second problem/domain supports the claimed scope
